subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• An icicle-shaped formation hanging from a cave ceiling is called a stalactite.
• A stalactite forms when mineral-rich water drips from the cave ceiling and deposits calcite, building up the formation layer by layer.
• Stalactites will gradually grow longer and thicker over thousands of years.
• A cave with long stalactites has experienced many centuries of mineral deposition, while a cave with short stalactites has experienced less.
• The Carlsbad Caverns in the United States contain many long stalactites.
prompt: The student wants to identify what causes stalactites. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Long stalactites are caused by many centuries of mineral deposition from the cave ceiling over time.
choices.B: The dripping and depositing of mineral-rich water from a cave ceiling forms stalactites, or icicle-shaped formations, over time.
choices.C: Over time, many long stalactites have formed in the Carlsbad Caverns, a cave system in the United States.
choices.D: The stalactites in the Carlsbad Caverns will continue to grow longer and thicker over thousands of years.

explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it directly identifies the causal mechanism behind stalactite formation. The sentence explains that stalactites form when mineral-rich water drips from a cave ceiling and deposits minerals, creating the icicle-shaped formations layer by layer over time. This answer synthesizes information from the notes to clearly convey the process that causes stalactites to exist, effectively accomplishing the student's rhetorical goal of explaining causation.
